I am 78 years old. I never went to school. I learned everything by doing it with my own hands and watching the older women in the village. My husband and I have 10 mu of land, just the two of us now. We have farmed here in Quzhou for 35 years. 

The 8 mu on the east and north sides I do wheat-maize, year after year. The wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October with shimai seeds, about 20 jin per mu, same as always. Before sowing I rotary-tilled and put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now that spring is here, I will topdress urea twice: half a bag per mu at green-up, and another half bag at heading. That is 50 jin of urea per mu total, which is 25 kg. I never cut back on fertilizer. Three years ago I tried saving money and used less — the wheat turned yellow and the ears were small. I lost money. Better to waste a little urea than to risk a bad harvest. I irrigate three times from my well: green-up water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. The well is good so I do not worry about water. I spray twice for medicine: once for weeds when it warms up, and once for aphids if they come. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, maybe a little more if the weather stays good.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to rest. I hire the machine service to plant maize directly into the stubble — no-tillage, no ploughing. The window is only a few days. I use hybrid seeds, nongda or denghai, whatever the dealer has that my neighbors bought last year. At sowing I put one bag of compound per mu. When the plants are knee-high I topdress half a bag of urea per mu — 25 kg. I water twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the grain is filling. Two sprays: herbicide at planting, and one for armyworms if I see them in July. I expect 1100 jin per mu of maize.

The other 2 mu I keep for cotton. Cotton is hard work for old hands like mine — picking every boll by hand — but the price was decent last year and I know this crop. I rotary-till in April and plant guoxinmian seeds. I put half a bag of compound per mu at sowing, then topdress 40 jin of urea per mu at flowering — that is 20 kg. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once when the bolls are growing. Cotton needs more medicine than grain: I spray four times, for bollworms, aphids, and red spiders. I hope for 500 jin of seed cotton per mu. If my back hurts too much during picking, I will ask my nephew to help for a few days.

I do what my neighbors do. If Lao Wang on the east side puts more fertilizer this year, I will probably do the same. I do not trust those people from the county who come with papers and talk. I trust what I see in the field. Fertilizer is expensive — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — but losing the whole crop is a disaster. I would rather spend the money.
